description:
Carried from round 2, still unaddressed. The manifest lookup grep -F "  ${ASSET}" is an unanchored substring match, so a manifest line naming a longer asset (e.g. 'gateship-darwin-arm64-next') would satisfy the lookup for ASSET=gateship-darwin-arm64. Not exploitable today (our own workflow generates the manifest from exactly the four TARGETS names, and an attacker who rewrites the manifest already controls the Release, as the README now says), and a multi-match would concatenate hashes and fail closed anyway. Still, this is the single line that decides whether a downloaded binary is trusted; grep -E "^[0-9a-f]{64}  ${ASSET}$" costs nothing and removes the class. The README's hand-verification snippet (README:97) has the same unanchored shape.

Source: cam/issue-495
Review round: 3

suggestion-fingerprint: 427f89a354e9

Carried from rounds 1 and 2. Every Release published so far predates SHA256SUMS.txt, so from the moment this lands on main the public curl|bash path (which is served live from main, not from a Release) fails with 'ERROR: download failed - .../SHA256SUMS.txt' until the next version tag is pushed, and GATESHIP_VERSION pinned to any older tag stays broken permanently. ADR-0057 explicitly accepts fail-closed and names this consequence, so this is diagnostic wording and merge/tag sequencing, not design: the message reads like a network problem rather than 'this release predates checksum publishing'. The README has the mirror-image gap, stating 'Every published asset ... carries an attestation from the release workflow' (README:113-115) when no currently published asset does; a 'starting with the next release' clause in each would keep both honest during the window.

Source: cam/issue-495
Review round: 3
